correctness.rationale: Stanković 2026 Theorem 1.1 proves fixed-index singular-value convergence, and Theorem 4.1 supplies each iterate's weak log-majorization by its input. For a_j=s_j(T)^p, decreasing b_j=s_j(Delta_t^n T)^p have b_k^k <= product_{j<=k}b_j <= product_{j<=k}a_j. Scalar AM-GM with k! >= ((k+1)/e)^k produces G_k <= e/[k(k+1)] sum_{j<=k} j a_j; telescoping gives sum G_k <= e sum a_j. Both b_j and limiting eigenvalue powers are dominated by G_j. Dominated convergence proves the p-power Schatten limit and the stronger ell_p distance statement. Zeros, finite dimension, 0<p<1, 0<t<1 and quasi-norm convention are covered. CHECK.py passed supplementary finite diagnostics and is not used to prove infinite results.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper formulates equal-exponent Schatten convergence as an open question. The new general theorem closes that exact gap for every p>0, including trace-class operators not belonging to any smaller Schatten class. It provides a uniform explicit input-dependent summable tail certificate and stronger ell_p convergence, a structural mechanism not afforded by ordinary fixed-coordinate convergence.
